miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.question: In Micah 7:19, God will cast all the people's sins into the depths of the sea.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.learningObjective: Observe where forgiven sins end up.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.feedbackCorrect: The final image is of sins cast far down into the deep.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread where the sins end up in Micah 7:19.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-01.hint: See where God casts the sins.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.question: In Micah 7:18, tap what God pardons in the remnant of his inheritance.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.feedbackCorrect: This is what the incomparable God pardons first.

feedbackWrong.a: "Transgressão" is also forgotten, but it comes later in this verse.
feedbackWrong.c: "Herança" (inheritance) is God's people, not what he pardons.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-02.hint: Look right after the opening question.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.question: According to Micah 7:18, why does God not hold on to his anger forever?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.learningObjective: Observe the reason for God's forgiveness.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.feedbackCorrect: The reason given is God's delight in being merciful.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not say he forgot the people.
feedbackWrong.b: Fear of the people is not the reason given.
feedbackWrong.d: Weariness does not appear; the reason is joy in forgiving.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-03.hint: Read the explanation at the end of the verse.

options.b: He fears how the people will react

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.question: Put Micah 7:19 in the order of the text.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.feedbackCorrect: Compassion, victory over wrongdoing and casting into the sea form the order.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-04.hint: The verse begins with God showing compassion.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.question: In Micah 7:19, what will God have on us before casting the sins into the sea?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.feedbackCorrect: God's tenderness opens the verse of forgiveness.

feedbackWrong.a: "Distância" (distance) is the opposite of merciful nearness.
feedbackWrong.b: "Orgulho" (pride) does not fit God's gesture here.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-05.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.question: What does Micah 7:19 say that connects to this context?
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.learningObjective: Connect forgiveness to the casting away of sins.
miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.feedbackCorrect: Here, forgiving means removing sin far away.

feedbackWrong.a: The sea is where the sins go, not a hiding place for the people.
feedbackWrong.b: The image does not store sins up to be charged later.

miqueias-sem-mq-05-mar-06.hint: See where the sins go in the verse.

options.a: People hidden at the bottom of the sea
options.b: Sins stored up to be charged later
options.c: Forgiveness that casts sins far away

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.question: In Micah 7:18, God does not hold on to his anger forever because he delights in showing mercy.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.feedbackCorrect: The cause is stated plainly at the end of the verse.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the link between anger and mercy in 7:18.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-01.hint: Notice the "porque" (because) at the end of the verse.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.question: In Micah 7:18, tap the word that links God's passing anger to his mercy.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.feedbackCorrect: This word introduces the verse's explanation.

feedbackWrong.a: "Sempre" (forever) marks duration, not the cause given.
feedbackWrong.c: "Como" (like) opens a comparison, not the final explanation.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-02.hint: Look for the word before God's delight.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.question: How does Micah 7:19 continue the idea of Micah 7:18?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.learningObjective: Relate mercy and the removal of sins.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.feedbackCorrect: The God who does not hold on to anger acts by casting sins far away.

feedbackWrong.b: Keeping sins contradicts casting them into the deep.
feedbackWrong.c: Forgiveness is not partial in where the sins finally end up.
feedbackWrong.d: Distance from God is not the movement of compassion.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-03.hint: See the action that comes after the compassion.

options.d: Compassion drives God away from the people

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.question: How does the celebration unfold in Micah 7:18–19?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.learningObjective: Understand how the celebrated forgiveness unfolds.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.feedbackCorrect: A question, forgiveness without lasting anger, and sins sent to the deep.

feedbackWrong.default: Casting into the sea closes the celebration.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-04.hint: The bottom of the sea is the end point.

options.a: God pardons the remnant of his inheritance
options.b: He does not hold on to anger forever
options.c: He casts the sins to the bottom of the sea

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-05.question: In Micah 7:18, what does God not hold on to forever against the people?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-05.learningObjective: Remember what God does not keep forever.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-05.feedbackCorrect: It lasts less than his delight in forgiving.

feedbackWrong.a: "Compaixão" (compassion) opens the next verse as God's gesture.
feedbackWrong.c: "Misericórdia" (mercy) is exactly what he delights in showing.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-05.hint: Look at what comes before the word "sempre".

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-06.question: What links Micah 7:19 to Psalms 103:12?
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-06.learningObjective: Relate forgiveness to the distance of sins.
miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts measure forgiveness by how far the sins are removed.

feedbackWrong.b: The distance shows removal, not a memory kept.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text brings sins near to be charged again.

miqueias-cam-mq-05-mar-06.hint: Compare the distance in both passages.

options.a: God removes our transgressions from us
options.c: Sins stay close to be charged later

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-01.question: According to Micah 7:18, God forgives the people but holds on to his anger against them forever.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-01.learningObjective: Evaluate the reading that makes God's anger eternal.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-01.feedbackCorrect: The celebration affirms precisely that his anger has a limit.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the sentence about anger in Micah 7:18.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-01.hint: Read what the verse says about God's anger.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-02.question: In Micah 7:20, tap the one to whom God will show faithfulness at the end of the book.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-02.learningObjective: Support God's faithfulness with the text.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-02.feedbackCorrect: This name opens the final promise of faithfulness.

feedbackWrong.a: "Abraão" receives the mercy mentioned next, not the faithfulness here.
feedbackWrong.c: "Nossos pais" (our fathers) is a general reference at the end, not the first named.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-02.hint: Look for the first proper name in the verse.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-03.question: What reading does Micah 7:19 support about forgiven sins?
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation of forgiveness in Micah 7:19.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-03.feedbackCorrect: Forgiveness removes sins to a depth beyond reach.

feedbackWrong.a: The image is not an easy-to-open file, but the deep.
feedbackWrong.b: Half forgiveness does not fit all of them being cast away.
feedbackWrong.c: Keeping them to charge later contradicts casting them into the deep.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-03.hint: Think of what happens to something cast far into the deep.

options.a: They become a file easy to review
options.c: They are kept to be charged later

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of Micah 7:18–20?
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-04.learningObjective: See the final forgiveness within God's story.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-04.feedbackCorrect: The ancient promise, Micah's question and deep forgiveness belong together.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the faithfulness promised to the fathers.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-04.hint: Follow from the ancient promise to the celebrated forgiveness.

options.a: God was faithful to Jacob and Abraham
options.b: Micah asks who is like God
options.c: Forgiveness casts sins into the deep sea

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-05.question: In Micah 7:20, what will God show to Abraham along with faithfulness to Jacob?
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-05.learningObjective: Remember the gift tied to Abraham.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-05.feedbackCorrect: The book closes by linking present forgiveness and an ancient promise.

feedbackWrong.a: "Compaixão" (compassion) appears in 7:19, not with this final name.
feedbackWrong.c: "Fidelidade" (faithfulness) is what is shown to Jacob in this sentence.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-05.hint: Look at the second proper name in the verse.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-06.question: What links Micah 7:18 to Isaiah 43:25?
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-06.learningObjective: Connect Micah's forgiveness to the God who blots out sin.
miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God himself takes the initiative to blot out the wrong.

feedbackWrong.b: Blotting out is not keeping things to remember later.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts, the initiative to forgive is God's.

miqueias-pro-mq-05-mar-06.hint: See who acts to blot out in both passages.

options.a: God blots out transgressions for his sake
options.c: The people blot out their own wrong

estudo:mq-05-mar.context: Near the end of the book, after announcements of judgment, Micah celebrates the incomparable God: he forgives, does not hold on to his anger forever, and casts sins into the depths of the sea.
estudo:mq-05-mar.focusQuestion: What sin do you need to let God cast far away, without fishing it back out?
estudo:mq-05-mar.keywordGloss: God delights in showing faithful kindness, forgiving instead of holding on to anger forever.
reflectionPrompts: Sins at the bottom of the sea
facts: God will show wonders as in the days of the exodus from Egypt.
God pardons iniquity and forgets the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance.
God does not hold on to his anger forever.
God will tread down iniquities and cast sins into the depths of the sea.
God will show faithfulness to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as he promised the fathers.
